# Shared acceptance vectors for the pinned `int(text)` / `float(text)` grammar.
#
# The Zig unit test (src/number_text_test.zig) and the native parity driver
# (tests/qbe_text.py) both read this table, so neither backend can drift from the
# other or from the documented grammar. One vector per line:
#
#     kind | input | outcome
#
# `kind` is `int` or `float`. `input` escapes with \s (space), \t, \n, \r,
# \v, \f, \\ and \uXXXX so every scalar survives a line-oriented file; an
# empty field is empty text. `outcome` is `none` when the text is not exactly one
# number, `nan` when the answer is a quiet NaN, and otherwise the exact value,
# written so that a correctly rounded decimal parser reproduces its bits.

# Integers: accepted
int|42|42
int|0|0
int|-0|0
int|+7|7
int|-7|-7
int|007|7
int|1_000|1000
int|1_0_0|100
int|\s\s8080\s\s|8080
int|\t\n42\r\n|42
int|\v\f5\v\f|5
int|9223372036854775807|9223372036854775807
int|+9223372036854775807|9223372036854775807
int|-9223372036854775808|-9223372036854775808
int|0000000000000000000000042|42
int|\u0034\u0032|42
